reason: Neither conversation asked the mandatory gas-smell or CO question; in both cases the homeowner volunteered the smell. Conversation 2 was more efficient and gave a plausible burner/aeration diagnosis, but it directed hands-on checks and told the homeowner to relight the burner before any safety screening, and its final emergency message omitted the Gas Safe engineer follow-up. Conversation 1's questioning was poor (repeated itself and asked about a 'programme' on a gas hob), but it issued no risky instructions and its emergency response was more complete, covering ECV, ventilation, 0800 111 999 and a Gas Safe engineer before reuse, so on a safety-first basis it edges ahead.
